newsitem.title: USA: Two US lawmakers want Congress to OK CPI changes.
newsitem.headline: Two US lawmakers want Congress to OK CPI changes.

text.p: Two House Democrats introduced a bill on Thursday that would require Congress to vote on any changes in the way the Consumer Price Index is calculated.

Representatives Jerry Kleczka of Wisconsin and Barney Frank of Massachusetts said the bill aims to make members of Congress accountable for any CPI changes that lead to cuts in cost-of-living adjustments for Social Security and other government benefits.
A congressionally appointed panel recently concluded that CPI overstates inflation by 1.1 percent a year.
But the Congressional Budget Office has said the index may overstate inflation by 0.2 to 0.8 percent.
Kleczka and Frank maintained that some members of Congress want to use the index as a tool for balancing the budget.

"This index has never been used politically before," Kleczka said at a news conference. "This bill does provide accountability." Frank said cutting back the cost of living adjustment is "one of the most socially regressive things the federal government could do."

Both lawmakers contended that other members of Congress would probably be reluctant to vote for changes in the way the CPI is calculated if the changes led to cuts in Social Security and other benefits.
